priors.applicability: Prefer when the drawer is open, the red block is exposed but displaced from its demonstrated pickup area, or execution enters before red release with a reliable current red pose. The robot and collision geometry must still admit the transformed targets. The caller identifies red, red_goal, and blue through closed typed arguments; their current observations are resolved at every replan.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer_position is strictly above 0.26 m, red is exposed, and a current red pose is available. Entry may be as early as the closed-gripper drawer-front state or later during red approach/contact/lift.
handoff.exit_conditions: Nominal switch after red is within the outside pad bounds and no longer follows TCP, followed by blue centered under TCP with closed fingers and observed blue/TCP co-motion on initial lift. These are handoff cues, not changes to task success.
handoff.failure_signatures: Red fails to co-move after closure, transformed approach is unreachable, red is carried into furniture, red remains outside the pad, red still follows TCP after opening, or post-release blue approach shifts with red rather than blue.
handoff.overlap_role: Preserves [230,470) supervision shared with open_drawer and [600,850) supervision shared with blue_insert. The first teaches drawer release through red lift; the second teaches red descent/release, retreat, blue approach/grasp, and lift.
handoff.successor_readiness: blue_insert can receive from index 600 with red still held/touching because release context is supervised, while the cleaner nominal switch is after established blue lift near the end of the cut.

Values are identifiers, not actuator commands, and all are rebound to current observations at each replan."}
priors.limitations: The exact equivariance is only with respect to the red pose frozen at each chunk replan; object motion within an eight-step chunk, pose-estimation error, unreachable transformed poses, furniture collision, and altered grasp physics are not solved. After red release, anchoring blue-transition targets to red is not blue-displacement invariant. Prefer the phase-conditioned TCP-relative prior for an uncertain post-release entry, and use the goal-centered prior when destination displacement or pad-relative placement is the dominant change.
priors.pipeline_implications: Use a standard independent DiffusionBackbone with two causal relational state frames and 10-D targets: red-frame XYZ metres, relative TCP rotation in continuous 6D form, and gripper scalar. encode_targets uses FK of demonstrated native commands and the chunk-start red pose; decode_action composes the sampled relative pose with that same causal red anchor, then calls the supplied IK from freshly measured joints. All twelve [230,850) cuts remain supervised, including both overlaps. No augmentation or auxiliary loss is needed; action diffusion remains the complete objective under the fixed 20k-update recipe.
priors.rationale: Observed: demo1000 approaches the red center by index 400, closes at 445, shows red/TCP co-motion at 470 and 500, carries near the pad at 560, descends by 600, and releases by 610. Demo1001 starts red at a different observed XY position, approaches that position at 400, and likewise closes/lifts/transports. Across the assigned data the red initial XY range is narrow, so an absolute world target can memorize it. Expected benefit: object-frame labels make the red-relative part of the demonstrated motion exactly equivariant to a changed observed red pose, rather than merely encouraging the network to infer that transformation. This is not evidence of recovery after a missed grasp.
priors.statement: Red-object equivariant Cartesian targets. Learn each commanded TCP target as a pose in the currently observed red-block frame at chunk construction, with red-frame translation, a 6D relative rotation, and the native-sign gripper scalar. This targets deployment displacement of the manipulated red block beyond the demonstrated initial range. The equivariance directly covers red approach, contact, grasp, and carried-red motion up to placement; translating or rotating red translates or rotates decoded targets before IK. Retain measured Panda qpos/qvel, fingers, drawer state, and red-relative TCP, goal, and blue relations so reachability, configuration, and scene dependencies are not discarded.

priors.applicability: Prefer when red has been acquired or is near acquisition and the observed red_goal/pad is displaced, or when accurate pad-relative descent and release dominate. The drawer must remain open and the requested goal must be reachable with clearance. The high-level caller selects the destination, carried object, and successor object identifiers.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer is open above 0.26 m; red is visible and preferably acquired or within demonstrated-style reachable approach; current red_goal is valid.
handoff.exit_conditions: Red lies within pad containment and ceases TCP co-motion; after supervised retreat, blue is under TCP with fingers closed and blue/TCP initial lift co-motion. These remain guidance only.
handoff.failure_signatures: Goal-relative descent is unreachable, red misses or tips outside the pad, fingers open before support, red follows retreat, retreat collides, or blue is approached at a stale absolute location.
handoff.overlap_role: Keeps open_drawer overlap [230,470) and blue_insert overlap [600,850), so destination-centered learning still sees drawer release/red pickup and predecessor release through blue pickup.
handoff.successor_readiness: The continuation from 600 explicitly includes final red descent/release before transit to blue. A nominal handoff at established blue lift is least ambiguous.

priors.invocation_contract: {"call_args_schema":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"destination":{"type":"string","enum":["red_goal"]},"carried_object":{"type":"string","enum":["red"]},"successor_object":{"type":"string","enum":["blue"]}},"required":["destination","carried_object","successor_object"]},"parameter_semantics":"destination selects the live observed red_goal world point, in metres, as the translational action origin; carried_object selects red for goal-relative state relations; successor_object selects blue for overlap conditioning. Identifiers are resolved from each causal observation and do not encode scripted poses."}
priors.limitations: No demonstrated goal relocation establishes collision-free or reachable execution at a new pad. A goal-relative output does not by itself solve a far-displaced red pickup, altered drawer geometry, grasp failure, or moving goal during a chunk. The blue handoff is not invariant to blue displacement. Prefer red-object equivariance for a displaced pickup and the phase-conditioned local prior for post-release or intermediate-state entries.
priors.pipeline_implications: Use an unchanged independent DiffusionBackbone. Two causal frames contain destination-centered scene geometry plus measured joints, velocities, fingers, and drawer state. The 10-D labels are red_goal-relative world-axis XYZ, absolute world rotation 6D, and gripper scalar. The decoder adds the current-replan goal translation, orthonormalizes 6D rotation, and invokes supplied IK from fresh joints. The model receives all twelve complete [230,850) segments and overlaps; no fabricated goal shifts are added, avoiding unsupported reachability/collision labels.
priors.rationale: Observed: in demo1000 the held red moves toward the fixed red_goal by 530-560, descends from high transport through 580 to near the pad at 594-604, and is left at z about 0.020 m while the gripper opens around 608-610 and retreats by 620-650. Demo1001 shows the same destination responsibility with a somewhat different red final XY/orientation and release timing. The demonstrations do not vary red_goal, so transfer to a moved pad is an expected benefit, not observed evidence. Encoding positions relative to the live goal makes translated placement/retreat labels transform predictably while world orientation and robot configuration retain feasibility dependencies.
priors.statement: Destination-centered placement targets. Express commanded TCP position as a world-axis offset from the currently observed red_goal and orientation as world-frame 6D rotation, plus gripper scalar. Goal-relative inputs expose red, TCP, and blue relationships while retaining qpos/qvel and drawer state. This prior targets displacement of the marked outside pad and pad-relative placement accuracy during carried-red descent, release, and retreat, with a different failure profile from red anchoring.

priors.applicability: Prefer when switching into the skill at an intermediate represented state, when red and blue approach poses could otherwise be confused, or when preserving local IK continuity from the current arm configuration is important. The high-level agent must choose phase from observable relations: drawer-front retreat before red contact; red grasp/transport/place while red is being approached/held; red release-to-blue after pad support and opening; blue pickup when TCP is near blue and closure/lift is intended.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer_position is above 0.26 m and phase is selected from current observable state. History remains two causal frames across a policy switch; only episode-start history may be duplicated.
handoff.exit_conditions: Terminate after red pad placement/release and, for the intended overlap, once blue is centered, fingers are closed, and blue/TCP co-motion indicates initial lift. Phase alone is not a grasp certificate.
handoff.failure_signatures: Caller phase disagrees with geometry, gripper closes on the wrong object, red lacks co-motion, red is off-pad or follows retreat, TCP revisits red after release, blue is not under TCP at closure, or IK reports an unreachable local target.
handoff.overlap_role: All actions in [230,470) and [600,850) remain covered. Coarse phase boundaries retain release actions on both sides of the successor overlap and include blue approach/contact/lift.
handoff.successor_readiness: blue_insert is callable from 600 with predecessor-release context. For this prior use red_release_to_blue through transit, then blue_pickup near the observed blue approach; clean successor readiness is established blue lift.

priors.invocation_contract: {"call_args_schema":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"phase":{"type":"string","enum":["drawer_release_to_red","red_grasp_transport_place","red_release_to_blue","blue_pickup"]},"primary_object":{"type":"string","enum":["red"]},"successor_object":{"type":"string","enum":["blue"]},"destination":{"type":"string","enum":["red_goal"]}},"required":["phase","primary_object","successor_object","destination"]},"parameter_semantics":"phase is high-level semantic intent bound to observable execution responsibilities, not elapsed time: drawer_release_to_red releases/retreats and approaches red; red_grasp_transport_place closes on red and carries/descends; red_release_to_blue opens, clears red, and transits toward blue; blue_pickup approaches/closes/lifts blue. Object and destination identifiers select current observed red, blue, and red_goal relations in metres/world poses."}
priors.limitations: A wrong phase argument can deliberately select the wrong object or gripper mode. Coarse boundaries include within-phase approach and contact variation, and local coordinates are not by construction invariant to a large red or goal displacement. Rotation-vector transfer assumes relative rotations remain away from the pi branch. Use the red-object prior for displaced red pickup and the destination-centered prior for moved-pad placement; none of the set proves grasp recovery, collision avoidance, or unreachable-state recovery.
priors.pipeline_implications: Train one independent unchanged DiffusionBackbone with a phase one-hot concatenated to two causal relational frames. Bind four contiguous ranges per demonstration—[230,445), [445,620), [620,780), [780,850)—so every assigned action and both overlaps remain supervised while phase semantics are explicit. Labels are 7-D chunk-TCP-relative translation, relative rotation vector, and gripper. decode_action composes with the causal chunk TCP, then uses fresh-joint IK. No recurrent phase memory or future state enters inference, and diffusion loss is the sole objective.
priors.rationale: Observed: both inspected demonstrations start with a closed gripper at the drawer front, open by 240, move through a long retreat/approach before red closure around 445, lift by 470, descend near 600, then release timing differs (demo1000 is opening by 608 while demo1001 remains closed at 610). Both then retreat/transit and approach blue, but their blue contact/lift timing and terminal height differ. These repeated geometric states with different intended objects create phase ambiguity, and adjacent skills may switch into any represented overlap state. Expected benefit: a coarse caller phase plus TCP-relative local targets conditions the mode explicitly and replans corrections from the actual intermediate TCP/configuration. It does not demonstrate recovery from unseen contact errors.
priors.statement: Phase-conditioned local Cartesian correction. Learn each target relative to the TCP pose at chunk construction: translation in that TCP frame, relative rotation vector, and gripper scalar. A required semantic phase argument selects one of four coarse responsibilities, while relational causal inputs and measured robot state retain geometry and reachability. This targets entry states produced at different points by adjacent skills and phase aliasing between red approach, red transport, post-release blue transit, and blue pickup.
